name: Stage Break Reading Series with Astra House
venue: McNally Jackson Books at Bklyn Studios
why: Four writers perform original short stories one page at a time, alternating with randomly selected audience readers; attendees get a printed zine of the four stories.

name: This Guy Sucked Presents: Draft of Shame
why: History podcast hosts use a sports-draft format to assemble a team of America's most notorious historical villains and pit them against each other.

name: Punch Puppet Slam: The Princess Bride
why: A diverse group of puppet artists use multiple puppet styles to perform The Princess Bride in a live variety-show format.

name: Live Band Karaoke at Arlene's Grocery
why: Sing your chosen song backed by a live full band (Nakatomi5); online ticket buyers enter raffles for drink tickets and free admission to future shows.

name: 13th Annual Americas Film Festival of New York
source: Americas Film Festival of New York
why: Festival of films from across the Americas exploring historical memory, migration, identity, childhood, and music; features screenings, documentaries, shorts, and filmmaker Q&As through October 9.

name: Georgia Gardner Gray: Cookie (Site-Specific Performance)
venue: Under the High Line, Meatpacking District
why: Site-specific performance staged in the former parking lot of the Meatpacking District's last meat purveyor, featuring grifters, fake tailors, and hustlers in a fever-dream narrative; runs through Friday.

name: Gather Round: Let's Dance – New York Swings (Final Night)
why: Final night of this free outdoor dance series: lindy hop and authentic jazz with choreographer Gaby Cook and Grammy-winning saxophonist Josh Lee, with a participatory dance component.

name: Bhangra in the Plaza
why: Weekly outdoor session of contemporary Indian music and dance featuring Sarina Jain and dancers from Masala Bhangra; all experience levels welcome. Runs Wednesdays through October 21.

name: Art21 Rewind: A 25th Anniversary Screening
why: Screening of artist documentaries from Art21's original 2001 debut season featuring Laurie Anderson, Mel Chin, Barry McGee, Shahzia Sikander, and others.

name: Infinite Good Times Movie Club: John Carpenter Double Feature
why: Double feature screening of John Carpenter's Big Trouble in Little China and They Live at a metal bar, with free popcorn and candy.

name: Charlene Kaye's 40th Birthday / King Mei Mei Debut Live Show
why: Debut live performance of Charlene Kaye's new glam-punk project King Mei Mei, coinciding with her 40th birthday celebration.

name: Mathematics and the Art of M.C. Escher (Exhibition Opening)
why: First major exhibition devoted to the mathematics of Escher's art, featuring 60+ prints, original woodblocks, and objects exploring symmetry, geometry, infinity, and impossible scenes; runs through Feb 8, 2027.

name: Archtober Festival
why: NYC's month-long festival of architecture and design with building tours, talks, workshops, exhibitions, and film screenings across the five boroughs with 100+ partner organizations; runs through October 31.

name: Rooftop Cinema Club (Fall Season)
why: Open-air rooftop movie screenings with wireless headphones, screening Halloween, Get Out, Ghostbusters, Hocus Pocus, The Exorcist, Rocky Horror Picture Show, and more through October.

name: The King of Japanese Kawaii: Sebastian Masuda in Conversation
why: Harajuku kawaii pioneer Sebastian Masuda discusses his colorful career and the culture he helped bring to the world in conversation with FIT professor Yuniya Kawamura.

name: DUMBO First Thursday Gallery Walk – Season Opener
why: Monthly self-guided walk through DUMBO galleries open late for receptions and artist talks, with outdoor projections and an after-party with DJ Nickodemus plus live saxophone and percussion.

name: The New York I Keep: An Evening of Obsessions
why: Five writers and thinkers each make a five-minute case for the one thing they can't stop loving about NYC, followed by a group walk outside to discover the city; speakers include Philip Lopate and Moses Gates.

name: Spoons, Toons + Booze: Halloween After Dark Edition
why: Halloween-themed cartoons from the 1940s–2000s on the big screen with sugary cereals and cereal-infused cocktails at this annual screening party.

name: China Now Music Festival – Opening Night at Carnegie Hall
source: China Now Music Festival / Carnegie Hall
why: Opening of the 9th annual China Now Music Festival: Huang Ruo and David Henry Hwang's opera The Rift plus three new works for the Bard East/West Ensemble blending Western strings with seven Chinese instruments.

name: Grand Central Terminal Tour with MAS Docents
source: Municipal Art Society of New York
via: Municipal Art Society of New York
why: Expert-led walking tour of Grand Central Terminal's architecture, history, and hidden spaces; multiple dates and times offered each week.

name: Guillaume Othenin-Girard: Drawing Into Place
why: Swiss architect and archaeologist Guillaume Othenin-Girard presents drawings in which architectural form, human narrative, and landscape are created through a single continuous line, blurring boundaries between place, memory, and imagination.

name: Kelly Walters for Open Flat File
why: Designer and educator Kelly Walters presents work inspired by The Hampton Album (1900) and the overlooked role of Black Americans in shaping American print culture, visual language, and design history.

name: Sawyer Avenue, Sunday Afternoon: Film Screening & Panel
why: Screening of a documentary about an immigrant family separated by immigration enforcement in a Chicago suburb, followed by a panel discussion on civil rights and immigration.

name: Praise Day for Sonia Sanchez!
why: Tribute celebration honoring poet Sonia Sanchez featuring Sweet Honey in the Rock, a poetry performance, and a community gathering with other prominent poets and artists.

name: Native Voices Karenna: Lay Our Vibration Down
why: Two short operas by Native American composers performed back to back, exploring indigenous voices in contemporary classical music.

name: John and Abigail Adams: The Modern Partnership at the Heart of the American Revolution
why: Reporter Jennifer Schuessler sits down with historian Lindsay Chervinsky and former Archivist of the United States Colleen Shogan to examine the founding couple's political partnership and Abigail Adams's complex views on the rights and role of women.

name: New York in the 1970s: When Music Saved the City (Panel + Disco Reception)
why: Pre-opening celebration for the 'You Should Be Dancing' exhibition: panel with MC Sha-Rock, Marky Ramone of the Ramones, Lenny Kaye of the Patti Smith Group, and DJ Nicky Siano, who revolutionized disco at Studio 54—followed by a live DJ set and disco reception.

name: You Should Be Dancing: New York, 1976 and Beyond (Exhibition Opening)
why: New exhibition charting the American bicentennial year through NYC's simultaneous cultural explosions—Ramones punk at CBGB, the birth of hip-hop in the Bronx, and disco's rise—set against the city's fiscal crisis.

name: Betye Saar's Black Dolls (Final Weekend)
why: Final weekend to see this exhibition honoring the centennial of Betye Saar's birth, including watercolors, assemblages, and her only self-made Black doll, Hoo Doo Woman (1974); exhibition closes October 4.

name: Submarines and Ironclads: Confederate Technology in the Civil War
why: Harold Holzer and Craig L. Symonds explore how the Confederate H. L. Hunley became the first submarine to sink an enemy warship, and how ironclads challenged Union naval dominance—part of the Leah and Michael Weisberg Series on American History.

name: Docent-Led Gallery Tour: Revolutionary Women
why: Docent-led tour of the museum's Revolutionary Women galleries; additional dates Oct 20 and Oct 24.

name: The Multi-Model Future: AI Engineering Panel (NYC)
why: AI engineering leaders from Brex, Baseten, Extend, and Vercel share what they've learned about choosing, routing, and running models efficiently at scale; one-hour panel then drinks with speakers.

name: Brderless Buildathon: AI Agents (Brooklyn)
why: 24-hour AI agent hackathon in Brooklyn followed by two weeks of continued shipping and a Demo Day—curated format where teams build a real product rather than just a demo.

name: Handcrafted Horrors Halloween Screening Series
why: Halloween screening series celebrating practical effects horror: Creature from the Black Lagoon in 3D, Fantasia, Faust, The Exorcist, Nosferatu with live musical accompaniment, Bram Stoker's Dracula, and more through October 31.

name: New York Film Festival at MoMI
source: Museum of the Moving Image / Film at Lincoln Center
why: Six NYFF selections screened at MoMI including Once Upon a Time in Harlem, Rose, Tender Loving Care, Bitter Christmas, Behemoth!, and The Only Living Pickpocket in New York; October 4–9.

name: MoMI After Dark Tours
why: After-hours tours of the Museum of the Moving Image with curated access and programming; limited spots for October 17.

name: MCNY Late-Night Wednesdays (Free Admission + Pop-Up Bar)
venue: Museum of the City of New York
source: Museum of the City of New York
via: Museum of the City of New York
why: Weekly free admission to all MCNY exhibitions on Wednesdays until 9 PM, plus a pop-up bar with signature cocktails and snacks; extended through the end of 2026.

name: Rare Look Inside M&S Schmalberg: NYC's Last Custom Fabric Flower Factory
why: Behind-the-scenes tour of M&S Schmalberg, the last remaining custom fabric flower factory in New York City, with a rare look at 100-year-old techniques still in use.

name: Private Lawn Bowling Workshop @ Central Park's New York Lawn Bowling Club
venue: New York Lawn Bowling Club, Central Park
why: Private hands-on lawn bowling workshop at one of Central Park's most hidden venues, the New York Lawn Bowling Club, which has operated on the same green since 1926.

name: Exploring the Grand Apartments of the Upper West Side
why: Walking tour of the Upper West Side's landmark apartment buildings—the Dakota, the Ansonia, the Apthorp—exploring their architecture, eccentric histories, and famous tenants.

name: Look Up! The Hidden History of NYC's Wooden Water Towers
why: Walking tour examining the wooden water towers that dot NYC's skyline—why they're still made of wood, how they work, and the craft behind the last family-owned businesses that build them.

name: Walking Brooklyn's Gowanus Canal: From Toxic Past to Luxury Living
why: Walking tour of the Gowanus Canal tracing its history from industrial wasteland Superfund site to luxury condo development, exploring the ongoing environmental remediation.

name: Alexander Hamilton's New York: Tracing the American Founding Father's Steps
why: Walking tour through the Lower Manhattan and Washington Heights sites most significant to Alexander Hamilton's life in New York, from his law office to his home to his burial place.

name: Tracing the Battle of Brooklyn: A Revolutionary War Battlefield Walk
venue: Prospect Park / Green-Wood Cemetery (meeting point TBD)
why: Walking tour of the site of the largest battle of the American Revolutionary War, tracing troop movements and key locations through what is now Prospect Park and Green-Wood Cemetery.

name: Exploring the Grand Mansions & Hidden Histories of Park Slope
why: Walking tour of Park Slope's Gilded Age mansions and brownstones, uncovering the neighborhood's history as one of the wealthiest districts in 19th-century America.

name: The Secret World of Flowers: Behind-the-Scenes NYC Floral District Tour
why: Behind-the-scenes tour of the NYC flower market district with access to wholesale vendors and insights into how millions of flowers flow through the city's floral industry each week.

name: The Abandoned Railway Urban Hike: Forest Park & the Future QueensWay
why: Urban hike along the abandoned Rockaway Beach Branch railway right-of-way through Forest Park, exploring the planned conversion to the QueensWay elevated park.

name: The Secret Eats of Arthur Avenue Food Crawl: The Bronx's Little Italy
why: Food crawl through the Bronx's Arthur Avenue, sampling Italian specialties from century-old butchers, bakers, pasta makers, and cheese shops in the city's most authentic Italian marketplace.

name: East Village, Rocks! Exploring the Neighborhood's Rock Music Legacy
why: Walking tour of East Village sites from the heyday of underground and alternative rock: CBGB's former location, the Velvet Underground's apartment, the Fillmore East, and more.

name: Exploring the Seaside Village of City Island
why: Guided tour of City Island, the Bronx's overlooked nautical village that feels like a small New England fishing town, with stops at its maritime history, boatyards, and seafood spots.

name: Exploring Andy Warhol & Truman Capote's Upper East Side
why: Walking tour following the footsteps of Warhol, Capote, Jackie Onassis, and other luminaries through the Upper East Side's art galleries, townhouses, and cultural landmarks.

name: Secrets of the East River: NYC's Hidden Infrastructure by Ferry
why: Guided ferry tour of the East River's hidden infrastructure—bridges, tunnels, power plants, and waterfronts rarely seen by New Yorkers—with expert commentary from aboard the boat.

name: Exploring Greenwich Village's Music History: From Dylan to Springsteen
why: Walking tour through Greenwich Village's folk revival landmarks: the Gaslight Café, Kettle of Fish, MacDougal Street clubs, and the apartments of Bob Dylan, Jimi Hendrix, and other icons.

name: Inside The Players with a Rare Look Inside Edwin Booth's Untouched Bedroom
why: Private tour of The Players, the landmark Gramercy Park club founded by Edwin Booth (brother of John Wilkes Booth) in 1888, including a rare look inside Booth's preserved bedroom.

name: Behind-the-Scenes @ The National Arts Club & 1844 Gilded Age Tilden Mansion
why: Behind-the-scenes tour of the National Arts Club inside the former mansion of Samuel Tilden, the 1876 Democratic presidential candidate—one of Gramercy Park's most stunning Gilded Age buildings.

name: From Crypt to Roof: After-Hours Tour @ The Cathedral of St. John the Divine
venue: Cathedral of St. John the Divine
why: After-hours private tour of the Cathedral of St. John the Divine—the world's largest cathedral—from its crypt to its roof, with access to areas closed to the public.

name: Exploring Dutch Lower Manhattan: From New Amsterdam to New York City
why: Walking tour of Lower Manhattan's Dutch-era sites: the original city wall (now Wall Street), the windmills, the first church, and the layers of history buried beneath modern streets.

name: The NYC Medieval Armored Combat Experience
why: Hands-on introduction to full-contact medieval armored combat: suit up in authentic period armor and learn the real techniques of sword fighting used by knights.

name: Supper Club with Pierce Abernathy: Ocean-Inspired Dinner + Short Film
why: Chef and slow-food advocate Pierce Abernathy hosts an intimate dinner centered on oceanic ingredients, paired with a screening of his short film about alternative seafood and farming solutions across NYC.

name: Second Sundays at Pioneer Works: Cuttlefish, Sugar Kelp & Marlon James
why: Monthly open house featuring live dwarf cuttlefish, community science with Seaweed City, Jean Painlevé's 1967 short The Love Life of the Octopus, open studios, and a launch event for Marlon James' new novel with a live set from Ragga NYC's Neon Christina.

name: Scientific Controversies No. 37: Octopus Umwelt
why: Janna Levin hosts comparative psychologist Dr. Alex Schnell and evolutionary biologist Dr. Caroline Albertin in conversation about what octopuses can teach us about consciousness, evolution, and the nature of intelligence.

name: Brooklyn Museum Fall Fête 2026
why: After-hours celebration of the opening season: performances by Otaku Choir, DJ Jon Ray, Acky Bright, Shia Ho, Angel Au, and wev!, hosted by Miss Ma'am She, plus late-night gallery access to new exhibitions including Cézanne to Modigliani, Art of Manga, and Hopi Kachina Dolls.

name: Art of Manga (Opening)
why: Major survey of manga as an art form, opening October 3 and running through January 31, 2027—featuring works from Rumiko Takahashi, Jirō Taniguchi, Tetsuya Chiba, Hirohiko Araki, and dozens more.

name: Open House New York Weekend 2026
price: Free drop-in at 158+ sites; $7 ticketed tours (release Fri Oct 2 noon)
why: Annual architecture and urban exploration festival unlocking 300+ sites across NYC—archives, artist studios, manufacturing spaces, landmarks—many drop-in and free; October 16–18, 2026.

name: OHNY Weekend: Port Infrastructure Boat Tour
why: Port Director Beth Rooney leads an up-close tour of New York Harbor's massive container ships and gantry cranes, with expert narration about the logistics of one of the world's busiest ports.

name: University Open Air at Prospect Park Boathouse
why: Weekend of free outdoor classes covering Tibetan yoga, food preservation, art, free will, AI, ornithology, and more; October 1, 3, and 4 at Prospect Park Boathouse.

name: JAY-Z IN 8 — HBO Documentary Screening (Episodes 5 & 6)
why: Free screening of episodes 5 & 6 of the HBO documentary JAY-Z IN 8—a candid, intimate conversation between JAY-Z and Rick Rubin marking 30 years since 'Reasonable Doubt.'

name: On Artistic Freedom: A Panel Discussion (Banned Books Week)
venue: Brooklyn Public Library, Central Library Dweck Center
why: Artist and author Christopher Myers, film producer Karin Chien, and publisher Namrata Tripathi (Kokila Books) discuss artistic freedom with Hyperallergic editor Hrag Vartanian—part of Banned Books Week.

name: UPRISING/DOWNFALL: Repression and Resistance in the Making of Democracy (Teach-In)
why: Four-hour teach-in featuring historians, activists, journalists, and authors examining American grassroots organizing—No-No Boys, Young Lords, ACT-UP, SNCC—with live music, performances, and readings from banned books.

name: NOU Film Festival at Flatbush Library
why: Afternoon of short films exploring migration, displacement, memory, identity, resistance, and belonging—from New York City to the Gambia, Finland, Jamaica, and across the African diaspora.

name: Traces of Gounouj (Site-Specific Dance, North American Premiere)
why: North American premiere of choreographer Léo Lérus' intimate 20-minute duet, performed three times across the afternoon on Governors Island—rooted in the Gwoka tradition of Guadeloupe and exploring intergenerational communication through movement.

name: Holy Ground: The Oyster (Governors Island)
why: Program exploring the oyster's central role in New York Harbor's ecology and history, as part of Governors Island's ongoing environmental programming.

name: BEBOP PORÚ at Six Coasts (Governors Island)
why: Live music event at Six Coasts on Governors Island—one of NYC's most unusual venues, a former officer's club with harbor views.

name: Pumpkin Point at Governors Island
why: Annual fall harvest celebration on Governors Island with pumpkins, autumnal activities, and seasonal programming.

name: High Holidays in the Tenements: Tour + Culinary Tasting
why: Tour of the Levine and Rogarshevsky family tenement apartments exploring how Jewish immigrants transformed Lower East Side storefronts and apartments into improvised synagogues for Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur—followed by a culinary presentation and tasting with culinary historian Sarah Lohman.

name: We the People: Democracy in the Tenements (Evening Tour)
why: Evening tour marking America's 250th birthday by tracing how tenement residents exercised democracy—the 1870 15th Amendment parade, the 1902 Kosher Meat Boycott, the 1974 bilingual education court case, the 1982 Chinatown garment workers' strike—followed by conversation and refreshments; also November 12.

name: Beaux Arts Ball 2026: Home Sweet Home
why: Annual party of the NY design community held at the historic 1924 Andrew Freedman Home on the Grand Concourse—a mansion built for formerly wealthy residents fallen on hard times—featuring an original installation by TAKK, DJs Bojaq and Madre Guia, and a dinner option.

name: NYC Yarn Crawl at Brooklyn Craft Company (Free Drop-In Workshops)
venue: Brooklyn Craft Company (Greenpoint + Lower Manhattan pop-up)
why: Both NYC Yarn Crawl locations offer free drop-in craft workshops (Scrappy Fabric Collage in Greenpoint; DIY Button Pins at the Lower Manhattan pop-up), plus 10% off all yarn Oct 1–4.

name: Intro to Woodcut Printing with Anat Keinan
why: Two-session introduction to relief printing on paper: image processing, ink mixing, block carving, and single and multi-layered printing in wood block and linoleum.

name: Water-Based Monotype Weekend Workshop
why: Weekend workshop in monotype printmaking—combining painterly gestures with layering on-plate elements, stencils, and cut paper drawings using non-toxic water-soluble inks. No prior experience needed.

name: Ancestral Ecologies: Archtober Sunset Tour
why: BBG's curatorial team leads a sunset tour of Ancestral Ecologies—four multisensory outdoor installations by Olalekan Jeyifous and AD--WO exploring Afrodiasporic and Latinx worldviews on ecology—closing October 25.

name: Louis Vuitton First Fridays at The Frick
why: Free after-hours Friday at the Frick: live jazz, drop-in drawing, drinks and bites in the Garden Court, gallery talks, and late access to the collection; monthly through May 2027 (Oct 2, Nov 6, Dec 4).

name: Miller Theater Pop-Up Concert Series (Season 15)
why: Sit onstage with virtuoso musicians for Columbia's hour-long early-evening concerts; free drink in hand, chance to mingle with performers after. Monthly through Dec 1.

name: New Museum Fall Exhibitions (Arthur Jafa: I Am Tony)
price: $28 general; free for SVA/NYU/Pratt; pay-what-you-wish Thursdays
why: Arthur Jafa: I Am Tony is the artist's most comprehensive survey to date, alongside The Bowery: Devil's Mile, Diego Marcon's Arrivederci Piggies!, and a site-specific video by Ho Tzu Nyen; through Jan 31.

name: 260 Madison Art Exhibition
why: 50+ artists occupy a former Duane Reade and 23,000 sq ft office floor in a Midtown tower under renovation, with works on surveillance, AI, extraction, and labor systems; through Nov 22.

name: NYTM Nostalgia Ride: Afternoon to Green-Wood Cemetery
why: Ride a vintage subway train through Brooklyn to Green-Wood Cemetery, then take a guided tour of the Victorian-era graves of famous actors, politicians, artists, and inventors.

name: Underground NYC Tour: Subway 101
why: Ride the subway with Transit Museum expert guides who reveal station secrets, art and architecture, and exclusive archival images from the Museum's collection.

name: Transit Walk: Gowanus and Carroll Gardens
why: Traces the transit history of NW Brooklyn including the Smith-9th Street station (one of the world's highest subway stations) and the Carroll Street Bridge, the country's oldest surviving retractile bridge.

name: Transit Walk: Downtown Brooklyn
venue: Downtown Brooklyn (walking tour ending at NYTM)
why: Traces Downtown Brooklyn's transit history from early ferry landings through trolley/el routes into the subway era, concluding at the Museum's historic Court Street Station.

name: NYC Secrets and Lies: Transit Tales
why: Three storytellers tell chilling tales from transit's mysterious past—but one is lying. Audience members who identify the liar enter a raffle for walking tour tickets. Halloween-season special.

name: Subway Swing: A Boogie for the Ages
venue: NY Transit Museum (1936 decommissioned subway station)
why: After-hours swing dance party with live jazz in the Museum's 1936 decommissioned subway station—vintage outfits encouraged.

name: Behind the Scenes: The Explorer's Club NYC Headquarters
why: All 5.5 floors of the 1904 members-only club's historic UES townhouse, with artifacts from scientific expeditions to land, sea, air, and space.

name: Backstage Metropolitan Opera House Tour
why: Exclusive access behind the curtain at the Met Opera: scenic and carpentry shops, wig and costume departments, rehearsal rooms, dressing areas, the Marc Chagall mural lobby, and the iconic auditorium.

name: Día de los Muertos at NYBG
why: Vibrant marigold blooms, a community ofrenda, playful puppets, crafts, and live music celebrate the Mexican holiday of memory and renewal across NYBG's 250 acres; through Nov 2.

name: Archtober Guided Tour of Little Island
why: Landscape Architect Signe Nielsen and Architect of Record Fabian Jabro—the designers who built the park—lead tours explaining how Little Island grew from a storm-damaged pier, the story behind the iconic tulip pots, and the thinking behind its paths and lawns.

name: Forging Ahead: Recent Acquisitions of Black Women Artists
venue: Schomburg Center for Research in Black Culture
why: 21 Black women artists working across media—exploring the iconography of the Black woman's body, futurism, spirituality, and the mapping of Black history—in new acquisitions to the Schomburg's permanent collection; through March 27, 2027.

name: Choosing the End: Ethics & Medical Aid in Dying
why: Jeffrey Kahn and Anna Mastroianni from the Johns Hopkins Berman Institute of Bioethics present an overview of the core ethical challenges around medical aid in dying for those facing terminal illness, including the debate over legalization and what autonomy means at end of life.

name: CBH Talk: Reimagining Filipino Brooklyn
why: Historian Michael Menor Salgarolo, filmmaker Claro de los Reyes (screening his 1940s-set Brooklyn waterfront short Sands Street), and Caroline C. Pasion explore the once-vibrant Filipino waterfront community around the Navy Yard that urban renewal and immigration policy erased.

name: Brooklyn Trivia with The Trivia Masters
why: Chris Kelley and Stuart Post of The Trivia Masters test the Brooklyn fold of your cerebral cortex with tough questions, lateral-thinking games, and multimedia challenges on Brooklyn history; come solo or assemble a team. Special guest: Brooklyn Borough Historian Asad Dandia.

name: CBH Talk: Haunted Brooklyn—Ghosts, Folklore, and the Stories We Tell
why: Halloween-season panel with Andrea Janes (Boroughs of the Dead ghost tours), Leila Taylor (Darkly), Colin Dickey (Ghostland), and novelist Victor LaValle examining how haunted-place lore—especially around Melrose Hall in Brooklyn—shapes our fears and the stories we need to tell.

name: Raise Your Voice: New York Activism (Puffin Foundation Center)
venue: Museum of the City of New York
source: Museum of the City of New York
via: Museum of the City of New York
why: Newly opened Puffin Foundation Center for NYC Activism inaugurates with this cornerstone exhibition on the history and legacy of civic engagement and social movements in New York City—successor to the long-running Activist New York.

name: He Built This City: Joe Macken's Model (Closing Oct 12)
venue: Museum of the City of New York
source: Museum of the City of New York
via: Museum of the City of New York
why: Last two weeks to see Joe Macken's extraordinary hand-built scale model of New York City featuring 800,000+ structures across all five boroughs—a viral sensation recently featured by the Associated Press.
